Definition: probably from G1670; an ulcer (as if drawn together):--sore.
BiblicalUsage: Helkos is a sore, an ulcer, and it appears three times, once in a parable and twice in judgment. In Luke 16:21 the dogs lick the sores of Lazarus at the rich man's gate, in Revelation 16:2 a grievous sore falls on the men who worship the beast, and in Revelation 16:11 they gnaw their tongues for pain and blaspheme God because of their sores.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the same word carries both pictures on purpose: the sores of the poor man God honours, and the sores of the rebels God judges; the difference is never the wound, it is who the sufferer belongs to.
